title: Edge refinement and color grading in a landscape edit (Patagonia series)

date.basis: embedded_creation_time in metadata suggests an export timestamp; transcript contains no explicit date.

summary: This video presents a step-by-step post-production workflow for a landscape image, focusing on darkening the foreground, expanding dynamic range, and then progressively revealing a brighter mountain behind with targeted color grading. The narrator explains selective lighting behind the mountain, edge refinement to keep edges flawless, and precise masking to prevent edits from creeping onto adjacent elements. The workflow also covers enhancing distant elements with blue tint to convey depth, bringing out fine detail in waterfalls with ultra-small brushes, and careful sky treatment to avoid over-contrasting the peaks. The transcript captures practical decisions about brush sizes, masking, and how to balance whites, blacks, and shadows to achieve a crisp, print-ready look.

sections.title: Initial framing, darken base, and prep
concepts: darkening foreground to manage dynamic range
setting up for subsequent tonal edits
sections.description: The session opens with adjusting composition by moving foliage into frame and cropping, followed by making the foreground notably dark to preserve dynamic range before introducing light back into the scene.

sections.title: Edge-based isolation and targeted adjustments
concepts: selecting and isolating the mountain behind
preliminary use of edge guides and masking
sections.description: Focus shifts to brightening the area behind the mountain and crafting a precise edge to prevent spillover. The editor discusses refining the edge and the idea of using guides (e.g., magnetic lasso) as a temporary aid to achieve clean separations.

sections.title: Color grading to separate planes and deepen depth
concepts: color grading tool for back lighting
enhancing top of the mountain and horizon
sections.description: With the edge refined, the workflow concentrates on adding warmth behind the mountain, then pushing a color grade to emphasize depth. The speaker emphasizes placing warmth centrally and behind the peak to create separation, while also introducing a blue bias to distant terrain.

sections.title: Fine-tuning depth with selective color and blue adjustments
sections.description: The editor uses selective color to heighten neutral separations and reinforces the blue hue in distant terrain, explaining the atmospheric reasons for the blue cast on far hills as distance increases.

sections.title: Detail enhancement of waterfalls and mid-tones
sections.description: A remarkably small brush (as small as four pixels) is deployed to accentuate waterfalls, followed by selective shadow dodging to push the waterfall and surrounding details forward while keeping mid-tones balanced.

sections.title: Light distribution behind the tree and sky considerations
concepts: whites as a control for light
preserving a smooth sky behind peaks
sections.description: Attention returns to areas behind trees to maintain light separation, with emphasis on whites to drive brightness and a hazy sky treatment behind peaks to avoid texture clashes with the mountains.

sections.title: Final considerations and potential future adjustments
sections.description: The speaker contemplates additional work behind the scene and reiterates the importance of a smooth sky behind high-contrast elements to preserve separation and avoid sky-to-peak texture conflicts.
